docs.title: Contents
docs.text:
EMIT Programming consists of workshops (called blast modules), seminars, and community-building events. Here we provide some resources for blast modules, career development, and summer school materials so that you can test and implement these programs into your department.

  • Blast Modules — summaries and materials when available
  • Whole Self Seminars — summaries of topics and materials when available
  • Summer School - curricula and materials
  • Resources — career development resources

docs.title: EMIT Summer School
docs.text:
The goal of the EMIT summer school is to provide students an overview of a growing field, opportunities to build community with other scientists, and resources for career development. The school is open to both local and visiting students, which provides an opportunity for these principles to be shared beyond our department. The school intentionally includes wellness sessions, open discussions, group projects, and breaks to model a balanced and inclusive academic atmosphere. After an overview of material and workshop sessions to learn various science tools and data analysis methods, participants spend the final week role-playing the project of attaining the first multimessenger detection of a massive black hole binary with LISA.

Each morning begins with a session dedicated to 'Student Stories.' This is an optional window for any participant (students, speakers, organizers, supporting staff) to spend a few minutes introducing themselves in any format they prefer. A sign-up space is provided in the schedule, and students are prioritized. This gives an opportunity for a student to promote their own science, share more about their hobbies or background, or tell a personal story. We find that it helps to have organizers and local participants sign up in the first week so that they can set the tone for these informal, flexible talks.

docs.title: Whole Self Seminars
docs.text: These seminars are intended to expand beyond the traditional science criteria and provide a more well-rounded and realistic scope of career development. Events ranged from talks from visiting professionals to group activities, discussions, and reading groups.

docs.title: How to conference
docs.text: This workshop provided students with vital information and pointers on how to promote themselves and navigate through certain conference settings. We discussed topics and scenarios they may encounter, which prepared a lot of our students for a large upcoming event they were attending. Discussion topics included: How attending conferences benefit you professionally and personally. Advice for introverts or first-time conference attendees at large vs small conference settings. Whether or not attending social outings, outside of conference agendas, are something of importance or not. How to unwind after a day of sessions to allow oneself to detach from “work mode”, decompress and fully enjoy themselves

docs.title: Vision Board
docs.text: This session was geared towards providing an opportunity for our students to get to know each other on more of a personal level. We discussed future goals and aspirations and the attendees were provided supplies to create their own vision boards to take with them.

docs.title: Unmasking Oneself
docs.text: This was facilitated by an esteemed Health & Wellness Practitioner/Educator and Lecturer from Cornell University, Jamilah Bey. She provided a very impactful personal/professional development teaching our attendees ways to gain a deeper understanding of how sometimes we all wear “masks” in certain environments and provided effective ways to gain the confidence to show up in professional/social settings just by being yourself unapologetically. This workshop also allowed individuals how to have more compassion for those who have different personalities than they do.
